classification.difficultyReason: Explain a half-life exponent, calculate the remaining percentage and use negative time to determine the original-to-present mass ratio.

content.prompt: [Decay of Uranium-235] Uranium-235 is a naturally-occurring isotope of uranium. It is particularly important because it can be made to fission, when it releases vast amounts of energy in a nuclear power station or a nuclear bomb. It has a half-life of about 700 million years, which means that if you store a mass of uranium-235 for 700 million years, half of it will then have decayed into other elements.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Explain why the mass of uranium-235 in the Earth $n$ years after the present is given by
$$M=M_0\times\left(\frac12\right)^{\frac{n}{700\,000\,000}},$$
where $M_0$ is the mass in the Earth now.

answer.short: There are $\dfrac{n}{700\,000\,000}$ half-lives in $n$ years, and the mass is multiplied by $\dfrac12$ each half-life.
answer.worked:
There are $\dfrac{n}{700\,000\,000}$ periods of 700 million years in $n$ years. Starting with mass $M_0$ and multiplying by $\dfrac12$ for each period gives
$$M=M_0\times\left(\frac12\right)^{\frac{n}{700\,000\,000}}.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The Andromeda Galaxy will collide with our Milky Way galaxy in about 4 billion years. What percentage of the present uranium-235 will still be present in the Earth? Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

children.label: c
children.prompt: The Earth itself is about 4.5 billion years old. How many times as much uranium-235 was present in the Earth when it was formed? Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.short:
$86.14$ times as much.

Use $n=-4.5$ billion years to calculate the original mass relative to the present mass.
answer.worked:
At the Earth's formation, $n=-4\,500\,000\,000$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{M}{M_0}&=\left(\frac12\right)^{\frac{-4\,500\,000\,000}{700\,000\,000}}\\\frac{M}{M_0}&=\left(\frac12\right)^{-45/7}\\\frac{M}{M_0}&=2^{45/7}\\\frac{M}{M_0}&\approx86.14\end{align*}$$
There was about $86.14$ times as much uranium-235.
